source.title: Fermanagh Herald, 4 June 1927, p. 5 ("Official Unionists defeated in Irvinestown and Lisnaskea")
source.publisher: Fermanagh Herald (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: Votes image-checked on the Fermanagh Herald page (Cathcart 493, Houston 213). The paper prints a majority of 275, but the printed votes give 280; no majority field is set because the printed figures are internally inconsistent.

note: Triennial election of Fermanagh County Council, polled Wednesday 25 May 1927 (Fermanagh Herald, 21 May 1927: 'The Local Government Elections will take place in Co. Fermanagh on Wednesday next, 25th May'). Three divisions were contested; the other seventeen divisions were uncontested; the Herald of 30 April 1927 prints the nominations and the winners are those left after withdrawals. Results declared at Enniskillen on Thursday 2 June (Fermanagh Herald, 4 June 1927). Structure and division names for the 1966-67 amalgamation are in notes/fermanagh-fcra-1969.md, from Fermanagh CRA, 'Fermanagh Facts' (1969). That is an advocacy pamphlet: use it for names only, not figures. Its register figures are disputed by Kingsley (2021) on the Omagh Rural District scheme. Read the page image before recording any number from it. Printed majority 275 does not agree with the printed votes (493-213=280). Both votes and the printed majority were read on the block image (FMH 4 June 1927, p.5); the newspaper figure is left as printed and the inconsistency noted.
